subject.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a shared residual durable-runtime boundary for cross-owner evidence and obligations, require a narrower owner-specific design, or decline this architecture direction?
rationale: The proposed contract creates future persisted-state, configuration, CLI, Gateway, and recovery ownership boundaries that cannot be validated or selected by documentation review alone.

options.title: Pause pending sponsorship
options.body: Leave this RFC unmerged until a maintainer explicitly owns the durable-runtime direction and its boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed RFC
options.body: Accept only a maintainer-defined residual fact set after confirming which existing lifecycle owners cannot safely represent it.

options.title: Keep ownership local
options.body: Decline the shared layer and require each cross-owner concern to use existing owner APIs or separately proposed extension points.

recommendation.title: Pause pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Leave this RFC unmerged until a maintainer explicitly owns the durable-runtime direction and its boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only visible non-author participant connected to this review cycle in the provided timeline.
